title: Dairy-Free Caramel Cupcakes
shortDescription: Dairy-free vanilla cupcakes with a coconut cream caramel swirl frosting, ready in about 45 minutes total.
description: These cupcakes started as a fix for my niece, who cannot have dairy but loves caramel more than anyone I know. I tested the caramel three times before it set up silky instead of grainy.
ingredients: 1/2 cup neutral oil (canola or light olive oil)
1 cup full-fat coconut cream, chilled and separated into solids
1/4 tsp flaky sea salt, for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat oil and granulated sugar together for 1 minute until smooth.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Alternate adding the flour mix and dairy-free milk, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners. Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
For the caramel, melt brown sugar and coconut cream solids in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir constantly for 5 minutes until it thickens and turns deep amber.
Pour caramel into a bowl and cool to room temperature, about 20 minutes, before using in frosting.
Beat dairy-free butter until fluffy, then add powdered sugar and half the cooled caramel. Beat 2 minutes until silky.
Pipe frosting onto cooled cupcakes. Swirl in the remaining caramel with a toothpick and top with a pinch of flaky salt.
tips: Chill your can of coconut cream overnight so the solids separate cleanly from the liquid.
Stir the caramel the whole time it cooks. It scorches fast once it starts to darken.
If your caramel seizes up, add 1 tablespoon of warm coconut cream and stir over low heat until smooth again.
Let the caramel cool fully before adding it to frosting, or it will melt the dairy-free butter.

faq.question: Can I use coconut milk instead of coconut cream for the caramel?
faq.answer: Use full-fat coconut cream, not coconut milk. Coconut milk has too much water and will not thicken into caramel properly.

faq.question: Why did my caramel turn grainy instead of smooth?
faq.answer: This usually means the sugar crystallized from stirring too slowly or too much heat too fast. Keep the heat at medium and stir the whole time.

faq.question: Can I make the caramel ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes, make it up to 3 days ahead and store in the fridge. Warm it gently before swirling it into the frosting.

faq.question: Is this recipe also vegan?
faq.answer: Not as written, since it uses eggs. Swap in 2 flax eggs if you want a fully vegan version, though the crumb will be slightly denser.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove dairy-free caramel can taste just as silky as the classic version. Make the caramel once and you will want to put it on everything.
